key_insight: MRI-derived finite element elastography showed potential to distinguish CKD from healthy kidneys without dedicated MRE acquisition.
engineering_relevance: The framework connects kidney geometry from conventional MRI to simulated viscoelastic responses and biomechanical features for computational disease assessment.
method: Convert kidney segmentation masks into watertight surfaces and tetrahedral FEM meshes.
Simulate harmonic waves using a nearly incompressible Kelvin–Voigt tissue model.
Estimate complex shear modulus via Helmholtz inversion and classify CKD using machine learning.
evidence_signal: FEM-derived stiffness was consistent with reported human renal MRE ranges, and classification reached 86.26% cross-validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.92.
watch_item: Stiffness is inferred from simulated rather than measured wave fields; the abstract reports no direct patient-level MRE validation.
paper_title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
